compound.project_id.note: Project identifier; the CIF itself calls the compound BTZP.

compound.chemical_name_casefile.note: Name assigned by dft/curate_cases.py. The CIF places H on N4 and N6 (the two outer triazole N) and none on N5, i.e. the 1H,3H-benzotriazolium cation (systematically 1H-1,2,3-benzotriazol-3-ium); check the name against the source paper before use.

compound.formula_moiety.value: C6 H2 N3 O7, C6 H6 N3
compound.formula_moiety.note: picrate anion C6H2N3O7(-), benzotriazolium cation C6H6N3(+)

xray.audit_block_doi.note: DOI of the CCDC data block

xray.mr.note: Multiwfn reports 348.22841 Da from its own atomic masses (data/r2/.../logs/mwfn_mep.out); quote the CIF value.

xray.space_group.note: CIF string "P2(1)/c"; Hall -P 2ybc; space-group No. 14 (standard numbering, not in CIF).

xray.symmetry_operations.note: Operation numbers 1-4 in this order are the first part of the n_klm symmetry codes used below.

xray.z_prime.note: derived: one cation + one anion (33 atoms) in the asymmetric unit, Z = 4 with 4 general positions

xray.software.note: The absorption-correction record names CrysAlisPro / SCALE3 ABSPACK (Oxford Diffraction) while _computing_* names Bruker SMART/SAINT: an internal inconsistency of the deposited CIF.

xray.hydrogen_treatment.value: mixed; every H atom has refined coordinates (with s.u.) and a refined Uiso
xray.hydrogen_treatment.note: N-H 0.91(4) (N4-H4N) and 0.83(4) (N6-H6N) Å; C-H 0.81(3)-0.96(4) Å: X-ray H positions are short, as usual.

xray.hbond_table_deposited.note: The CIF has no _geom_hbond_* loop. All hydrogen-bond geometries below are computed here from the deposited coordinates and symmetry (derived).

xray.hb02_N6_H6N_O6.note: derived; acceptor at symmetry 3_666 = (-x+1, -y+1, -z+1); donor at x,y,z; intermolecular; not in the DFT cluster

xray.hb06_C3_H3_O3.note: derived; acceptor at symmetry 1_555 = (x, y, z); donor at x,y,z; intramolecular (picrate), S(5)-type C-H...O(nitro) contact with a near-100 deg angle; not a hydrogen bond by the usual angle criterion; not in the DFT cluster

xray.hb_search_criteria.value: H...A < 2.9 Å and D-H...A > 100 deg, acceptors N/O, all images within +-2 cells
xray.hb_search_criteria.note: The cluster builder (dft/build_cluster.py) uses stricter criteria: H...A < 2.65 Å, angle > 130 deg, heavy-atom clash < 2.40 Å.

xray.asu_closest_interion_contact.note: derived; the two moieties of the asymmetric unit are not hydrogen bonded (N5 carries no H), which is why the cluster was rebuilt from a symmetry image

xray.asu_closest_interion_distance.note: derived; matches the 2.99 Å quoted in the case-file notes

xray.stacking_triazole_cg_cg.note: derived; centroid-centroid distance between the triazole ring and its inversion image (3_565 = -x, 1-y, -z); rings parallel

xray.stacking_triazole_perp.note: derived; perpendicular separation of the two parallel triazole planes

xray.stacking_note.value: no picrate...cation or picrate...picrate ring centroid pair closer than 4.3 Å

model.n_electrons.note: Multiwfn: 178 electrons (89 alpha, 89 beta); fmo.json n_electrons 178, n_occ 89

model.fragments.value: picrate anion: 18 atoms (atom indices 0-17, C6H2N3O7); benzotriazolium cation: 15 atoms (indices 18-32, C6H6N3)

model.atom_order.value: CIF atom order within each ion, picrate first (indices 0-17), then cation (18-32); the CIF itself interleaves the two ions (O1, N3, O7, N4, C6, ...). Cation labels carry the internal suffix #4_666 (never show it in the paper)

model.symmetry_cation.note: derived: operation 4 (x, -y-1/2, z-1/2) plus lattice shift (1,1,1). Equivalent, seen from a cation at x,y,z: the picrate at 4_465 = (x-1, -y+1/2, z-1/2).

model.defining_hbond.value: N4-H4N...O1 (cation N-H to picrate phenolate O)
model.defining_hbond.note: Chosen by dft/build_cluster.py (exhaustive search over symmetry images, H...A < 2.65 Å, angle > 130 deg); the bifurcated N4-H4N...O7 (123 deg) is also inside the cluster but below the builder angle cutoff.

model.missing_hbond.value: N6-H6N...O6 (to a second, inversion-related picrate at 1-x,1-y,1-z) is not represented
model.missing_hbond.note: In the cluster N6-H6N is a free N-H; see xray.hb for its crystal geometry. "Inversion-related" refers to the asymmetric-unit frame (donor cation at x,y,z): that picrate is the inversion image 3_666 of the asymmetric-unit picrate. Relative to the picrate actually in the cluster it is the 2_1-screw image 2_746 (2-x, y-1/2, 3/2-z), H6N...O6 2.103 Å (fact-check, derived).

model.n_basis.note: also fmo.json n_basis, Multiwfn "Basis functions: 606", molden 606 functions

model.basis_per_element.value: C, N, O: 22 functions each (5s4p1d, spherical d); H: 7 functions (4s1p)
model.basis_per_element.note: derived by counting shells in the molden; 25 heavy atoms x 22 + 8 H x 7 = 606

model.basis_overrides.note: no basis_overrides key (unlike PZC, which uses def2-TZVP on Zn)

pcm.n_lindep_removed.note: "3 small eigenvectors of overlap matrix removed" at the final PCM geometry (603 MOs; molden padded to 606 with zero vectors). 4 were removed at some earlier PCM frames (optimize.log: 41 x 4, 30 x 3).

model.preopt_basis_functions.source: basis-set count: 6-31G(d) with spherical d functions, 25 heavy atoms x 14 + 8 H x 2
model.preopt_basis_functions.note: B3LYP/6-31G(d) pre-optimisation size; derived check: 25 x 14 + 8 x 2 = 366 with spherical d

protocol.functional.value: B3LYP (PySCF xc="b3lyp" = libxc HYB_GGA_XC_B3LYP, ID 402, VWN-RPA local correlation, same definition as Gaussian)
protocol.functional.note: No B3LYP_WITH_VWN5 override exists anywhere in the repository.

protocol.aux_basis.note: INFERRED, NOT VERIFIED FROM A RUN LOG (SCF verbosity 3 hides the choice). Per the PySCF 2.14.0 source, Pople 6-311++G names are reduced to "6311++g", which DEFAULT_AUXBASIS maps to aug-cc-pVTZ-JKFIT for hybrid functionals, unless BSE metadata supplies a JK-fit set first. Write "the default auxiliary basis chosen by PySCF" unless confirmed.

protocol.grid_level.source: verify_grid.log (dft/verify_grid.py run, not deposited); run_case.sh (GRID_LEVEL default 4)
protocol.grid_level.note: Known issue: every RESULTS.md says "grid level 3" - wrong. verify_grid.py matched grid 4 for btpc_gas (stored E reproduced to 0.00 microHa; grid 3 differs by 1.5 microHa). btpc_pcm was NOT in the verify run; grid 4 for it rests only on the run_case.sh defaults. The "grid 4" in the btpc_pcm opt.xyz comment is a literal string written by dft/finalize_opt.py, not a recorded setting, so it is not independent evidence.

protocol.grid_points.value: H: 60 radial x 434 angular (Lebedev order 35); C, N, O: 90 radial x 590 angular (order 41); Treutler-Ahlrichs radial, Becke partition, NWChem pruning
protocol.grid_points.note: from the PySCF source, not from a run log

protocol.pcm_lebedev_order.note: 302 points per atomic sphere. dft/common.py (PCM_LEBEDEV_ORDER default) still says order 17 (the 3ATB Mac setting) - superseded. verify_grid.log confirms Lebedev 29 for 3atb_pair_pcm and pzc_pcm; btpc_pcm itself was not verified.

protocol.pcm_radii.value: modified Bondi radii (H 1.10, C 1.70, N 1.55, O 1.52 Å) scaled by 1.2 -> H 1.32, C 2.04, N 1.86, O 1.824 Å
protocol.pcm_radii.note: PySCF defaults (not overridden in dft/common.py); from source, not logged

protocol.pcm_discretisation.value: SWIG (switching-Gaussian) surface, no probe radius, electrostatic term only (no cavitation/dispersion/repulsion)

protocol.scf_conv_tol_final.note: single points for frequencies, FMO/analysis wavefunction and every displaced gradient

protocol.optimizer.value: geomeTRIC 1.1.1 via pyscf.geomopt.geometric_solver, TRIC coordinates: 99 (= 3N) delocalised internals built from 170 primitives (34 bonds, 35 angles, 17 out-of-plane, 72 dihedrals, translation + rotation of each ion), trust radius 0.1 (max 0.3) Å, maxiter 300

protocol.opt_criteria.value: |dE| < 1.0e-6 Ha, RMS grad < 3.0e-4, max grad < 4.5e-4 Ha/Bohr, RMS disp < 1.2e-3, max disp < 1.8e-3 Å (all five required)
protocol.opt_criteria.note: geomeTRIC defaults, equal to Gaussian default thresholds. btpc_gas met all five; btpc_pcm did not (see pcm.opt_*).

protocol.preopt.value: B3LYP/6-31G(d) with loose criteria (dE 1e-6, grms 1.7e-3, gmax 2.5e-3, drms 6.7e-3, dmax 1.0e-2) - pipeline default
protocol.preopt.note: For BTPC the final grid-4 runs skipped this stage and started from preopt.xyz files carried over from earlier grid-3 runs on the OVH VM (see gas.opt_start, pcm.opt_start); the 6-31G(d) stage happened in those earlier runs (not in the archive).

protocol.hessian_method.value: central finite differences of analytic gradients (6N = 198 gradients), each displaced SCF started from the converged density

protocol.hessian_projection.value: translations and rotations projected out in mass-weighted Cartesians (QR-orthonormalised projector), own routine dft/vibrations.py
protocol.hessian_projection.note: residual 2.7e-5 (PCM), 2.8e-5 (gas) cm-1. PySCF harmonic_analysis listed the PCM imaginary mode as 0+3.2j and counted it as real (n_imaginary_pyscf = 0).

protocol.thermo_p.note: PySCF rigid-rotor/harmonic-oscillator thermochemistry, no low-frequency correction

protocol.fmo_descriptors.value: IP = -E_HOMO; EA = -E_LUMO; chi = (IP+EA)/2; mu = -chi; eta = (IP-EA)/2; S = 1/(2 eta); omega = mu^2/(2 eta)
protocol.fmo_descriptors.note: Koopmans-type. Softness convention S = 1/(2 eta) (some papers use S = 1/eta, which doubles S). Values from the PCM wavefunction include the continuum reaction field.

protocol.fragment_composition_method.value: Mulliken partition of each MO over the two fragments: sum over fragment AOs of c_mu (S c)_mu

protocol.cubes.value: HOMO/LUMO/density 80^3, ESP 64^3, margin 4.5 Bohr (2.38 Å) beyond the outermost nuclei (PySCF cubegen); render isovalues: orbitals +-0.02 a.u., MEP on 0.001 a.u. density, NCI RDG = 0.5 coloured -0.035..+0.02 a.u.
protocol.cubes.note: PySCF cubegen takes margin in Bohr: every cube origin equals the smallest nuclear coordinate minus 4.5 Bohr on each axis (e.g. PCM x: -8.1537 - 4.5 = -12.6537 Bohr). The "4 A"/"4.5 Å" wording in dft/fmo.py is wrong. The 0.001 a.u. surface extends at most ~1.8 Å beyond the nuclei (Multiwfn vertex ranges), so it is not clipped.

protocol.mep_surface.value: Multiwfn main function 12: electron-density isosurface 0.001 a.u., grid spacing 0.25 Bohr, marching tetrahedra; ESP evaluated exactly at surface vertices
protocol.mep_surface.note: Colour range of the rendered MEP = surface min..max (mep_range.json). Reported MEP numbers do not depend on the 64^3 ESP cube (render only).

protocol.mep_esp_code_pcm.note: Multiwfn exited with code 59 after writing complete output; accepted by dft/mwfn.py

protocol.mep_esp_code_gas.note: LIBRETA fast (2) and slow (3) both segfaulted (exit 174) on the gas wavefunction; code 1 ran 863 s, exit 59, output complete; statistics then parsed separately (STAGES 2026-09-17 00:31).

protocol.mep_note.value: The ESP is that of the (PCM-polarised, for btpc_pcm) molecular charge density alone; the PCM surface charges are not part of the mapped potential
protocol.mep_note.note: derived from how the analysis was run

protocol.nci_settings.value: Multiwfn 20 -> 1 (NCI), "High-quality grid" covering the whole system with 1.5 Bohr extension; RDG_maxrho = 0.1 a.u. (points with rho >= 0.1 set to RDG 100); promolecular approximation not used (full wavefunction)
protocol.nci_settings.note: Default RDG_maxrho is 0.05; raised to 0.1 (setup_linux.sh) so the short N-H...O bond survives (its critical-point density is 0.087 a.u. in the gas phase, gas.bcp_H4N_O1_rho).

protocol.nci_spike_method.value: dft/mwfn.py:nci_post: sign(l2)rho binned from -0.200 to +0.050 a.u. in 0.001 bins; a bin is a candidate if it holds >20 points and its minimum RDG < 0.3; contiguous candidate bins are merged and represented by the bin with the lowest RDG; type label: < -0.015 "attractive (H-bond)", < +0.010 "van der Waals", otherwise "steric repulsion"
protocol.nci_spike_method.note: The label is purely a threshold on sign(l2)rho; assignments to atoms are in *.nci_region_* facts (derived here).

protocol.elf_lol_settings.value: Multiwfn 4 -> 9 (ELF) / 10 (LOL), plane through three atoms, 300 x 300 points, aug2D = 6.0 Bohr, Becke definition (ELFLOL_type 0, ELF_addminimal 1)

protocol.elf_plane_picrate.value: picrate ring plane through C6, C4, C2 (1-based Multiwfn atoms 4, 9, 6)

protocol.elf_plane_cation.value: benzotriazolium plane through N4, N5, C7 (1-based atoms 19, 23, 21)
protocol.elf_plane_cation.note: triazole and benzo rings are coplanar (9-atom rms deviation 0.0009 Å PCM, 0.0013 Å gas), so one map covers the whole cation

saddle.interpretation.value: The PCM stationary-point search ended on an almost flat inter-ion libration coordinate: over the last 30 steps the ions rotated by ~38 deg for 0.30 kcal/mol, the residual imaginary frequency (3.2i cm-1) belongs to that same rigid-body motion and survived a doubled FD step. The intra-ion geometry and the N4-H4N...O1 bond are converged; the relative orientation of the two rings is not determined to better than a few tens of degrees.

lit.pk_picric_acid.note: thermodynamic pK of picric acid in water at 25 C (davis1963spectrophotometric)

lit.pk_picric_acid_spread.note: spread of earlier picric acid pK determinations (davis1963spectrophotometric)

lit.pka_benzotriazolium_flash.note: pKa of the N-protonated benzotriazolium cation, flash photolysis, I = 1.0 M (wang2000photochemistry)

lit.pka_benzotriazolium_older.note: basicity pKa of benzotriazole from the older review quoted by Alkorta et al. (alkorta2012theoretical)

lit.dpka_picric_acid_flash.note: derived: pKa(BTAH+) 0.42 (flash photolysis, I = 1.0 M) - pK(picric acid) 0.33 (25 C)

lit.dpka_picric_acid_flash_range.note: derived: 0.42 minus the spread 0.2-0.8 of published picric acid values

lit.dpka_picric_acid_older.note: derived: basicity pKa 1.6 of the older review quoted by Alkorta et al. - pK(picric acid) 0.33

lit.dpka_picric_acid_range.note: derived: lowest (flash-photolysis value, highest picric acid value) to highest (older value, lowest picric acid value) Delta pKa over the published values; printed as "about -0.4 to 1.4"

pcm.hessian_step_bohr.note: finite-difference displacement step of the reported Hessian

gas.hessian_step_bohr.note: finite-difference displacement step of the reported Hessian

saddle.hessian_step_first_bohr.note: step of the first IEF-PCM Hessian (the check)

rev.proton.scan.level.value: B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p), no dispersion, density fitting, grid level 4, Gas phase; every coordinate relaxed except r(H4N...O1), held by a geomeTRIC distance constraint; GAU (Gaussian defaults, as dft/optimize.py)
rev.proton.scan.level.note: dft/revision/proton_scan.py; four chains: up (1.46-1.70 A) and down (1.40-1.08 A) from the published gas-phase minimum, neutral (0.98-1.28 A) from a start with H4N on O1, and the O-side extension (0.90, 0.94 A) added on 22 Nov after the first DVR run found the O-side well unbracketed

rev.proton.scan.coordinate.note: the scanned (constrained) coordinate: the H4N...O1 distance; r(N4-H4N), r(N4...O1) and the angle relax

rev.proton.scan.n_optimisations.note: constrained optimisations in the four scan jobs (every one converged on the Gaussian default criteria); plus the single point at the published minimum (chain min)

rev.proton.scan.n_points.note: points of the profile: one per target distance (the lower-energy chain where two chains reached the same target) plus the published gas-phase minimum

rev.proton.scan.labels.note: profile points, N side (large r(H4N...O1)) first; the order of every rev.proton.scan.* and rev.proton.gas.*.dE_kcal list

rev.proton.scan.r_HO_A.note: r(H4N...O1) at each profile point (order of rev.proton.scan.labels); B3LYP optimised geometries

rev.proton.scan.r_NH_A.note: r(N4-H4N) at each profile point (order of rev.proton.scan.labels); B3LYP optimised geometries

rev.proton.scan.r_NO_A.note: r(N4...O1) at each profile point (order of rev.proton.scan.labels); B3LYP optimised geometries

rev.proton.scan.NHO_deg.note: angle N4-H4N...O1 at each profile point (order of rev.proton.scan.labels); B3LYP optimised geometries

rev.proton.scan.delta_A.note: r(N4-H4N) - r(H4N...O1); > 0: proton nearer O1 at each profile point (order of rev.proton.scan.labels); B3LYP optimised geometries

rev.proton.scan.max_constraint_dev_A.note: largest |r(H4N...O1) - target| over the 20 constrained optimisations

rev.proton.scan.max_opt_steps.note: largest number of optimisation steps of one scan point (limit 100)

rev.proton.scan.hysteresis_max_kcal.note: largest energy difference between the down chain (from the salt) and the neutral chain (from the neutral start) at the 5 shared targets [1.08, 1.13, 1.18, 1.23, 1.28] A: no hysteresis, the two branches meet

rev.proton.scan.min_vs_published_Ha.note: reproduction check: tight single point at the published gas-phase minimum vs the published energy

rev.proton.scan.transfer_r_HO_A.note: r(H4N...O1) where r(N4-H4N) = r(H4N...O1) on the relaxed path (linear interpolation between neutral_1.280 and down_1.230)

rev.proton.scan.lumo_on_picrate_pct.note: B3LYP LUMO, Mulliken share on the picrate atoms (H4N counted with the cation fragment), per profile point: on the cation down to r(H4N...O1) = 1.28 A, on the picrate (picric acid) from 1.23 A

rev.proton.gas.lowest_point_r_HO_A.note: the lowest-energy profile point (neutral_0.980, H4N on O1) is the same at every level, B3LYP, wB97X-D3(BJ), M06-2X, PBE0, CAM-B3LYP, DF-MP2 and SCS-MP2 (HF alone has its lowest point at 0.94 A)

rev.proton.gas.ionic_point_r_HO_A.note: the published B3LYP gas-phase ionic minimum (profile point min), the reference of every dE_kcal list

rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.dE_kcal.note: B3LYP: E(point) - E(published B3LYP ionic minimum geometry), per profile point (order of rev.proton.scan.labels); B3LYP tight single points of the scan job itself

rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.dE_ionic_minus_neut.note: B3LYP: E(salt, published B3LYP ionic minimum geometry, r(H4N...O1) 1.437 A) - E(neutral, lowest profile point, r(H4N...O1) 0.98 A); positive = the neutral form lies lower. Electronic energies along the B3LYP path, no zero-point or thermal terms

rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.ionic_well.note: B3LYP: does the profile have a local minimum with the proton on N4 (a point lower than both neighbours, r(N4-H4N) < r(H4N...O1))? Judged on the computed points, not on the interpolating spline (the spline of dvr.py shows spurious 0.0003 kcal/mol dips for M06-2X and PBE0)

rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.ionic_min_r_HO_A.note: B3LYP: r(H4N...O1) of the lowest N-side point (min)

rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.barrier_r_HO_A.note: B3LYP: r(H4N...O1) of the highest point between that minimum and the O side (down_1.230)

rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.well_depth_kcal.note: B3LYP: depth of the ionic well = E(down_1.230) - E(min), barrier to proton transfer from N4 to O1 on the computed points

rev.proton.gas.wb97xd3bj.dE_kcal.note: wB97X-D3(BJ): E(point) - E(published B3LYP ionic minimum geometry), per profile point (order of rev.proton.scan.labels); single point at the B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) relaxed-scan geometry (6-311++G(d,p), density fitting, grid level 4; DF-MP2 frozen core, RI basis aug-cc-pVTZ-RI; SCS-MP2 = 6/5 OS + 1/3 SS of the same job)

rev.proton.gas.m062x.grid5_abs_max_kcal.note: M06-2X: largest change of the absolute energy from grid level 4 to 5 at the three checked points (neutral_0.980, neutral_0.940, neutral_0.900)

rev.proton.gas.m062x.grid5_rel_kcal.note: M06-2X: change of the relative energy of the two O-side points from grid level 4 to 5

rev.proton.dvr.settings.value: sinc-DVR (Colbert-Miller) on the 16-point profile of each level; coordinate xH = arc length of the path of H4N after superposing consecutive scan geometries on all other atoms, zero at the lowest point; mass of H (1.00782503207 u); cubic not-a-knot spline, continued 0.30 A beyond each end with the end slope and curvature, then a hard wall; 801 grid points; 6 levels

rev.proton.dvr.pad_A.note: extension of the potential beyond the scan

rev.proton.dvr.x_range_A.note: xH of the first (r(H4N...O1) 1.70 A) and last (0.90 A) scan point

rev.proton.scan.x_A.note: DVR coordinate xH of each profile point (order of rev.proton.scan.labels); the same for every level

rev.proton.dvr.m_eff_path_u.note: effective mass (u) of the whole relaxed path = (mass-weighted path length / proton path length)^2: the heavy atoms move a lot along the path, so the 1-D model with the mass of H is the light limit and the mwpath variant (unit mass on the mass-weighted path) the heavy limit

rev.proton.dvr.selftest.value: 5 of 5 passed (harmonic, morse, sampled_harmonic, double_well, sampled_double_well)
rev.proton.dvr.selftest.note: analytic checks of the DVR code run in the same job: harmonic and Morse levels, a spline-sampled harmonic potential, symmetric and asymmetric double wells

rev.proton.dvr.first_run_p_outside_pct.note: superseded first DVR run (14 points, 0.98-1.70 A): its lowest point was the O end, so 24 % of the ground state lay outside the scan; this led to scan_gas_oside (0.90, 0.94 A). Not to be quoted as a result

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.zpe_cm.note: B3LYP: ground proton level v = 0 above the minimum of the interpolated potential

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.fundamental_cm.note: B3LYP: first excitation E(v=1) - E(v=0) along the proton path

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.v1_kcal.note: B3LYP: level v = 1 above the potential minimum

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.p_O_v0_pct.note: B3LYP: probability of the ground state on the O side (r(N4-H4N) > r(H4N...O1), the neutral form) (value from the recomputation in rev/proton.py, unrounded; equal to the stored 5-decimal value within 6e-6)

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.p_O_v1_pct.note: B3LYP: the same for v = 1 (value from the recomputation in rev/proton.py, unrounded; equal to the stored 5-decimal value within 6e-6)

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.p_outside_v0_pct.note: B3LYP: ground-state weight outside the scanned range (in the extrapolated pads); dvr.py flags > 1 % (value from the recomputation in rev/proton.py, unrounded; equal to the stored 5-decimal value within 6e-6)

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.grid_conv_cm.note: B3LYP: largest level change from 801 to 1601 grid points (dvr.py warns above 1 cm-1; the change is below 0.4 % of the ZPE)

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.spline_undershoot_k.note: B3LYP: depth of the spline minimum below the lowest computed point (the DVR zero); dvr.py flags > 0.2

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.transfer_above_v0_k.note: B3LYP: potential at the point r(N4-H4N) = r(H4N...O1) minus the ground level; positive = the ground level lies below the half-way point of the transfer

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.neutral_min_r_HO_A.note: B3LYP: r(H4N...O1) of the minimum of the interpolated potential (O side), interpolated from xH

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.ionic_min_above_v0_.note: B3LYP: bottom of the ionic well (spline, r(H4N...O1) 1.434 A) above the ground level; positive = the ionic minimum lies above the zero-point level, so it holds no bound proton state of its own

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.barrier_above_v0_kc.note: B3LYP: barrier top (spline, r(H4N...O1) 1.232 A) above the ground level

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.v1_minus_barrier_kc.note: B3LYP: level v = 1 relative to the barrier top

rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.well_depth_spline_k.note: B3LYP: ionic-well depth on the interpolating spline (compare rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.well_depth_kcal)

rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.ionic_min_r_HO_spli.note: B3LYP: position of the ionic minimum on the spline

rev.proton.gas.b3lyp.barrier_r_HO_spline.note: B3LYP: position of the barrier top on the spline

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.verdict.value: double well: ionic minimum 0.98 kcal/mol above the ground level; ground state 99.4 % on the O side
rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.verdict.note: B3LYP: summary; ionic minimum judged on the computed points (dvr.py verdict for M06-2X and PBE0 reports a spline dip of 0.0003 kcal/mol as a second minimum: a spline artefact, not used)

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.sens_zpe_cm.note: B3LYP: ZPE per DVR variant: main (xH, mass of H, cubic, extrapolated walls), pchip interpolation, box walls at the scan ends, reduced mass H against N+O, coordinate [r(N-H) - r(H...O)]/2, coordinate -r(H...O), mass-weighted path with unit mass (heavy-atom limit)

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.sens_p_O_v0_pct.note: B3LYP: ground-state O-side probability per DVR variant (names as sens_zpe_cm)

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.sens_p_O_v0_min_pct.note: B3LYP: lowest O-side probability over the variants (variant rHO); the -r(H...O) coordinate with the mass of H compresses the path to half its length and so overstates the zero-point spread

rev.proton.dvr.b3lyp.sens_p_O_v0_min_exc.note: B3LYP: lowest O-side probability over the variants other than rHO (variant half_delta)
